shilka.initial:
Edit image1 Shilka: change ONLY the painting/rendering style to match images2 Harrier and3 F22 from the SAME game's accepted aircraft set. Preserve image1 exact silhouette, short gun lengths, all six road wheels, four gun barrels, circular rear radar, all component positions, angle, framing, transparent background. Do not reshape or add components.
The current Shilka looks like a stylized plastic scale model: thick cream edge strokes, outlined raised panels, individually shiny rounded bolts, uniform flat cel-like plate fill and overly black seams. Remove those stylistic traits. The target aircraft have physically credible military metal, thin unobtrusive panel seams, low contrast restrained surface wear, subtle continuous light gradients across planes, directional upper-left light and soft local metal reflections. Match that painting technique exactly on the Shilka's actual geometry. No cartoon linework, no bevel-highlight tracing every edge, no thick dark contours around panels, no heavy black ring around turret, no gold or cream rim. Keep hardware shapes but render bolts and hinges as small low contrast real fasteners. Repaint gray-olive military metal in the same neutral gray/olive family as Harrier, with gentle plane transitions and sparse fine abrasion, clean silhouette. Broad top surfaces reflect a soft muted light, side surfaces slightly darker, tracks dark but readable. Do NOT copy aircraft camouflage layout, insignia, gold canopy, numbers, wings or aircraft parts onto the vehicle. Keep image1 modest small reddish access plate. Retain readable side-on vehicle at 80px hull width while using aircraft style, not a simplified icon. One complete vehicle only, no text, no background, no floor shadow. Transparent output.
shilka.correction:
Precise style correction of image1 Shilka. The previous edit merely added mottled texture and retained the bright outlined plastic model appearance. This edit must visibly FIX that. Image2 Harrier is the target metal shading.
Preserve every pixel-level geometric feature, vehicle silhouette, component positions, pose, framing and transparent background. Repaint surfaces only. REMOVE the pale cream line tracing the turret hatch perimeter, top rectangular strips, hull hatches, wheel rims and radar rim. Blend those edge strokes into adjacent metal until nearly invisible; only small subtle directional reflections at few corners. Reduce tiny bolt highlight contrast by 70%. Tone down overly black borders surrounding access panels to very thin faint seams. Suppress the blotchy crackle/grunge texture over large faces by at least 80%, retain sparse directional wear instead. Broad surfaces should have soft continuous directional metal shading like the Harrier, not flat cel panels, not raised outlined blocks, not random dirt. Modest neutral gray olive paint, avoid making whole vehicle darker. No added marks or changed shapes. A credible hand-painted military vehicle in the exact realistic rendering language of the accepted Harrier aircraft, with smooth metal light transitions and restrained detail. No aircraft camouflage transferred, no writing, no backdrop, no shadow outside vehicle.

tunguska.initial:
Edit image1 Tunguska to use the SAME painting technique as accepted HeavyMach aircraft images2 Harrier and3 F22. Image1 fixes geometry only. Preserve silhouette, left-facing pose, exact short barrel lengths, six road wheels, missile tubes, turret/radar positions, transparent framing. Make no geometry additions.
Repaint military gray-olive metal with softly varying continuous light and realistic thin panel seams, as in the aircraft references. Eliminate the toy-like appearance: remove continuous bright cream strokes along plate edges and wheel rims; soften each raised-panel bevel, each fastener highlight and the jet-black outline around every hatch. Keep mechanical seams but thin and low contrast, not drawn contour lines. Lower extreme cavity darkness at turret ring while keeping attachment obvious. Panel faces need gentle upper-left illumination and subtle slightly uneven worn paint, neither flat cel-shaded patches nor noisy procedural grunge. Tracks are dark graphite with restrained small metal highlights, wheels look painted metal rather than glossy rounded plastic. Moderate fine wear like Harrier; do not cover every panel in scratches. Neutral gray with faint olive tint, no gold or warm ivory border. No aircraft parts, camouflage pattern, insignia, numbers or gold canopy transferred. No floor shadow or scenery. Single complete transparent side-view sprite, restrained surface depiction suitable at 85px hull width. Match rendering language across aircraft and ground vehicle, not just hue.
tunguska.correction:
Edit image1 Tunguska surfaces only; preserve entire exact silhouette, all components, short guns, six wheels, framing and transparent alpha. Image2 Harrier defines the accepted HeavyMach metal painting language. Image3 corrected Shilka shows ground vehicle consistency.
The preceding Tunguska still has a white rim around every hatch and a uniformly speckled rough surface. Make plate edge highlights much softer and interrupted, not continuous cream linework. Reduce pale contrast on wheel rims and bolt heads. Thin and soften drawn dark outlines around hatches. Keep real welded/mechanical structure but render it through subtle metal lighting, not outlined beveled shapes. Remove most evenly distributed mottling and crackle noise on the radar, turret and hull side. Replace with quiet slightly worn gray olive paint with gentle continuous upper-left metal shading and only sparse fine scuffs. Avoid flat cel-shaded color patches. Aim for physically credible sheet metal with the Harrier's subdued surface variation, coordinated with corrected Shilka. Keep tracks darker than hull but readable, no plastic shine. Do not change geometry, add symbols, aircraft livery, gold stripes, labels or scenery. Output one whole vehicle on transparent background.
